Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office maintains a central register of submitted forms, assigns sequential identifiers, and stores scanned copies in a digital archive. Staff log each intake event with a timestamp, route items to the responsible division via internal tracking fields, and update status codes upon review or closure.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared a draft inspection summary on a standard form and modified the "Deficiency Count" field from a plural numeric entry to "0". The actor changed the "Overall Status" field from "Failed" to "Passed" and appended a dated certification field attributed to a named examiner account. The actor transmitted the document via a direct messaging channel to a recipient account, then submitted the altered document to the records portal, overwriting the original submission ID in the archive index.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor accessed the records portal using named staff credentials and opened the digital archive directory. The actor retrieved the original inspection form, a prior certification template, and the account roster listing examiner identifiers. The actor used a document editor and a messaging application to stage the changes and communicate the revised outcome.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The archive retained the original file hash alongside the modified submission hash. The audit log recorded two consecutive save events with a short interval, both attributed to the named staff account. The messaging channel contained a transfer of the revised document and a reference to a payment transaction identifier. The status field in the tracking system showed a change from "Open" to "Closed" without an intermediate review entry.
